annual_frequency.note: value = Anne Arundel County NRI v1.20 hurricane annualized frequency (0.0941); NRI range across the four counties 0.0941-0.1035. high = HURDAT2 rate of tropical-storm-strength passages within 100 nm of Annapolis 1975-2024 (0.38/yr). HURDAT2 cross-check computed for this memo (center 38.98N 76.49W, Annapolis; any storm status, max interpolated wind inside radius): 1975-2024, 7 storms at >=34 kt passed within 50 nm (0.14/yr: Danielle 1992, Bertha 1996, Ernesto 2006, Hanna 2008, Isaias 2020, Zeta 2020, Ida 2021); 19 within 100 nm (0.38/yr); 3 at hurricane strength within 100 nm (0.06/yr: Gloria 1985, Floyd 1999, Irene 2011). 1851-2024: 0.155/yr (TS within 50 nm), 0.063/yr (hurricane within 100 nm). Isabel 2003 never came within 100 nm of Annapolis (closest ~115 nm) yet produced the record Bay surge. Countywide/area frequency, not per-building damage probability.

perils.severity_note: Tropical systems reach this market weakened, but wind-driven rain through failed flashings and edge metal is the main roof mechanism, and embedded tornadoes are common (Ida 2021). NRI v1.20 cut Anne Arundel's hurricane building EAL to $7.93M/yr (v1.19: $36.1M), rating Relatively Moderate. Roughly 3 tropical-storm-strength passages within 50 nm expected per 20-year roof life (HURDAT2, 1975-2024 rate).

perils.severity_note: The feature that distinguishes Millersville from Laurel: NRI rates coastal flooding Relatively Moderate in all four counties. Hurricane Isabel (Sep 18-19 2003) drove an unprecedented Chesapeake surge of 7+ ft; the Annapolis gauge recorded its record 7.2 ft MLLW; downtown Annapolis, the Naval Academy and Baltimore's Inner Harbor/Fells Point flooded; ~60 mph gusts and >500,000 customers without power in central MD; ~$820M damage in MD/DC (search excerpts of NWS/Wikipedia). Surge is not a roof peril itself, but surge events coincide with sustained wind and wind-driven rain, and they flood rooftop-equipment electrical feeds and ground-level mechanicals.

roof_age_underwriting.text: Reused from Laurel research (Maryland statewide). Carriers increasingly treat roof age and condition as a primary factor in insurability, pricing and terms. Common structure: roofs ~0-10 years old at replacement cost; 10+ years moved to a roof payment schedule (prorated by age); ~15+ years may be actual cash value (ACV) only for wind/hail. Maryland brokers note older buildings sometimes need roof (and electrical/plumbing) updates before a carrier will quote. Most published roof-schedule material describes personal lines; commercial roof schedules and ACV roof endorsements exist but thresholds are carrier-specific, so there is no Maryland-published standard. For PaxSeal: documented inspections and repair records are the evidence an underwriter asks for when a roof is past 10 years.

wind_hail_deductible_norms.text: Reused from Laurel research, plus Bay-shore specifics. Percentage wind/hail deductibles are common in commercial property: typically 1%-5%, applied per building/location (endorsement removes the per-occurrence deductible), calculated on the building limit or on the loss depending on form (ISO CP 03 21 Windstorm or Hail Percentage Deductible). In this market hail is a Very Low NRI hazard, so the practical issue is named-storm/hurricane and windstorm deductibles for tropical remnants and derechos. No Maryland-specific survey of deductible levels found. For Millersville the Bay shoreline adds named-storm/windstorm deductible and flood questions: a broker page states the Maryland Joint Insurance Association (MDJIA, the state FAIR plan) commercial program applies a 5% windstorm/hail deductible (search excerpt; the '$100,000' qualifier in the excerpt is ambiguous and unverified). Flood (surge) is excluded from commercial property forms and requires NFIP or private flood cover; one consumer site quotes NFIP premiums of $900-2,200/yr for Chesapeake/Anne Arundel shoreline properties (residential-oriented excerpt, low confidence).

code_triggers.text: Reused from Laurel research (Maryland statewide), with Anne Arundel specifics. (1) Code basis: Maryland Building Performance Standards (COMAR 09.12.51) require every jurisdiction to enforce the same I-code editions; the 2021 IBC/IRC/IECC/IEBC were adopted statewide effective May 29 2023, with local enforcement required by May 29 2024. Maryland published proposed 2024 I-code adoption in the Maryland Register on June 26 2026 (comments closed July 27 2026), so a 2024-code cycle is imminent. Howard County has already adopted the 2024 suite locally. (2) Recover limits (IBC 1511.3.1.1): a roof recover is NOT permitted where the existing roof/covering is water-soaked or deteriorated to the point it is not an adequate base, or where the existing roof already has two or more applications of any covering; in those cases a full tear-off is required. This is the direct link between neglect and cost: trapped moisture from unrepaired leaks turns a recover/restoration option into a full tear-off. (3) Energy code on re-roof (IECC C503.3.1, 2021): roof replacement on a roof with insulation entirely above deck must meet the prescriptive insulation (C402.1.3/.4/.5 or C407) for the climate zone (4A here); total R-value may not be reduced; minimum 1 in. at drains/scuppers. A Baltimore cost source cites R-25 to R-35 polyiso at $2.00-3.50/sq ft, a large add-on to a tear-off. (4) Damage thresholds: no Maryland- or county-specific percentage-of-damage rule forcing full replacement (like Florida's 25% rule) was found; IEBC repair provisions apply. Anne Arundel/Annapolis: search excerpts of local contractor pages state the 2021 IBC is in force in Anne Arundel County (adopted by Maryland May 29 2023, enforced by all jurisdictions since May 29 2024), and that Anne Arundel County Inspections and Permits requires a permit for commercial roof replacement. Baltimore City and Baltimore County were not separately checked. Flood-zone buildings: FEMA/IEBC substantial-improvement rules can apply to Bay-front buildings where repair cost exceeds 50% of building value, but no Anne Arundel-specific interpretation for re-roofs was found.
